blocks.text: SINGAPORE — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Thursday said negotiations for a Code of Conduct in the South China Sea were making “good progress,” expressing optimism that the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) and China could reach an agreement to prevent maritime confrontations from escalating. Marcos said the proposed agreement was crucial to managing tensions in the disputed waters, warning that a mistake by a sailor or soldier could trigger a wider confrontation. “We’re working very, very hard, we’re making good progress as a matter of fact, in terms of the code of conduct,” Marcos told Forbes Chair and editor-in-chief […]...
